2020.change_reason: First available year; it sets the baseline of headline-driven community and product news under a 'Building a Responsible Foundation' tagline.
2020.analyst_notes: Brief news-feed copy with a corporate-citizenship tagline ('use our growth for the greater good') backed by a concrete $9.25 million Charlotte-area commitment. Otherwise the page is mostly headlines and navigation, so few stated values are visible.

2021.change_reason: The featured headlines changed (a military-family commercial, a Remembrance Trail project, a private-brand carpet launch), while the responsibility tagline stayed the same.
2021.analyst_notes: Story-driven and warm, with emphasis on military families and product launches. The claims are episodic and carry no metrics.

2022.change_reason: Featured content moved to a $100 million five-year Hometowns commitment, a sustainability report and an LGBTQ-owned vendor spotlight, replacing the 2021 military and product stories.
2022.analyst_notes: The most concrete page so far ($100 million over five years, a Corporate Responsibility Report), though the page itself reports no outcomes. The vendor story is a DEI signal but appears as a single news item.

2023.change_reason: Sustainability and vendor items dropped out, replaced by community projects (Build it Forward, a gardener story) and an internship story.
2023.analyst_notes: Human-interest storytelling about community and careers. The claims are anecdotal and contain few measurable commitments, so specificity is lower than in 2022.

2024.change_reason: Featured stories shifted to associate and partner stories (an associate's assistance story, a Messi partnership), with the Hometowns season the only community item.
2024.analyst_notes: Tone shifts to associate-centered and sponsorship marketing. The personal-story framing is more emotional than the earlier program and dollar claims, and the page contains no metrics.
